conflicts.fact: Whether learners' initial ideas (fish old / no food) are treated as fully ruled out or still partly valid; Lesson 7 lists predators and competition (food) as contributing factors
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says old age or lack of food cannot explain the phenomenon. Lesson 7 ranks competition for food and predation among nine candidate factors and says they work together with nutrients to cause the decline.

conflicts.fact: Which question closes Lesson 1 and how Lesson 2's content relates; also Lesson 1 says habitat adaptations are next although it includes tilapia and Nile perch as river fish while Lesson 2 classes algae as hydrophytes
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 treats algae as producers within the river community. Lesson 2 groups algae and weeds with hydrophytes (plants), although algae are not hydrophyte plants.

conflicts.fact: Cause of the smell and role of oxygen: Lesson 7 lists algae cover as reducing light and oxygen, while Lesson 8 attributes smell to anaerobic decay after algal death
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7: extra nutrients cause algae and weed growth that reduces light and dissolved oxygen. Lesson 8: algae and weeds die, decomposers use up oxygen and anaerobic decay produces foul smell.
